chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Fadala ibn Ayoub, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send any Prophet at all except that it was in the Knowledge of Allah, Blessed and High, that when He completed His Religion for him, among it would be the prohibition of wine, and wine never ceased to be unlawful. Rather, the Religion changes from one characteristic to another, and had that (change) been in its entirety, they (people) would have been cut-off from the Religion.
ai.seo_question: Was wine always prohibited in Islam or was it introduced later?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'Tahdith al-Ahkam' (changing of rulings), clarifying that the prohibition of wine was eternally known to God and never fully abrogated, but rather its legal manifestation shifted from a gradual transition to a final, absolute decree. It underscores the Shia understanding that divine law evolves to accommodate human capacity, ensuring continuity of guidance rather than abrupt discontinuation. This perspective highlights the wisdom behind the phased revelation of rulings, such as the transition from the initial prohibition of wine to its complete ban in Surah Al-Ma'idah.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, form Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, 
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not Send a Prophet<sup>as</sup> at all except it was in the Knowledge of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High that when He<sup>azwj</sup> Completes His<sup>azwj</sup> Religion for him<sup>as</sup>, among it would be the Prohibition of the wine, and the wine will never cease to be unlawful. But rather, the Religion changes from one characteristic to another, and had that (change) been in its entirety, they (people) would have been cut-off to be without the Religion’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah abu Ayyub from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said,

’Every time Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent a Prophet, it was in the knowledge of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, that in the case of completing His religion wine must have been made unlawful. It had to remain unlawful, however, religion is to change the habits one after the other. Were such change to take place at once people would boycott religion as a whole.’”
